077025 SPC is listed as a special non-contributory benefit for the purposes of EC law 1. Such benefits are
only payable in, and at the expense of, the State in which the person is habitually resident. This means
that SPC is payable in the UK only and EC law does not permit export of this benefit to claimants living
abroad.

                                                                1 Reg (EC) No. 883/04, Art 70; and Annex X

DMG 77140–77184 distinguish the mixed-age definition, Universal Credit interaction, excluded-partner exceptions and effective dates. The general exclusion is not the complete rule. DMG memo 04/24 paragraphs 15–17 add a protected mixed-age migration route from 8 June 2024: the specified protected couples sent a migration notice may reclaim pension-age Housing Benefit or claim Pension Credit within three months after the relevant UC or HB award ends. That route requires its stated prior entitlement and migration facts; it is not a general right for every mixed-age couple. 77016 A polygamous marriage case is one in which1


1. a person (the person in question) is a husband or wife by virtue of a marriage entered into in a country
which permits polygamy and


2. either party to the marriage has for the time being any spouse additional to the other party and


3. the


         3.1 person in question and


         3.2 other party to the marriage and


         3.3 additional spouse


         are members of the same household.


Note 1: The DM should obtain evidence of the marriage, if a claimant declares more than one spouse.


Note 2: See DMG 77140 et seq where one or more members of a polygamous marriage are mixed-age.

Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"Maximum savings credit

77363 The MSC is1 a fixed percentage of the difference between the


1. SMG and


2. SCT.


Note: See Appendix 1 to this Chapter for details of the rates.


                                                                 1 SPC Act 02, s 3(7); SPC Regs, reg 7(1)(a)


Example 1 - Claimant who has a partner


Edna, who is aged 65, claims SPC for herself and her partner Paul. At the time of her claim, the
appropriate SMG is £160.95, the SCT is £127.25 and the fixed percentage is 60%. The MSC for Edna is
£20.22 (£160.95 SMG - £127.25 SCT = £33.70 x 60% = £20.22).


Example 2 - Claimant who has no partner


Finlay is aged 67 and has no partner. At the time of his SPC claim, the appropriate SMG is £105.45, the
SCT is £79.60 and the fixed percentage is 60%. The MSC for Finlay is £15.51 (£105.45 SMG - £79.60
SCT = £23.85 x 60% = £15.51).
